name: Washburn
summary: Barry County, MO: a 100-foot steel fire tower finished in 1955 on land bought in 1944; the record lists it gone and no source found dates the removal.
design: 100-foot steel fire tower with a small cabin at the top, finished in 1955 to replace a wartime pole-type or wooden tower
status_note: The record lists the tower as gone. No source I found dates its removal or describes the towersite today.
agency: Missouri Conservation Commission, later the Missouri Department of Conservation

events.note: Missouri Conservation Commission buys a 40-acre towersite four miles west of Washburn (Pineville Democrat, September 7, 1944)
100-foot steel tower completed in September 1955 (Neosho News) to replace a temporary pole-type (wooden) tower from the war years
Bobby Lawrence, transferred from the Joplin tower, named to man the new tower (Neosho News, September 1955)
Old tower residence dismantled and a new building constructed (FY 1956-57 report)
April 2, 1961 grass fire pushed by a strong wind; Wayne Lawrence, 50, found dead; his brother Bob was an observer at the tower (Jefferson City Post-Tribune)
